correctness.rationale: For labeled H(3,3), the 27 vertices, 81 edges and explicit 1296-element wreath-product automorphism action enumerate all 2925 triples into ten disjoint orbits, with power-forcing success on exactly three specified orbits. Independent brute-force closure and orbit-based closure algorithms check all 27 singletons, 351 pairs and 2925 triples. All 1296 optimal states and their single-replacement edges are explicitly constructed and two independently implemented BFS strategies determine all 839160 unordered optimum-state distances under each move rule. Degree, edge, radius, diameter, antipode and same-endpoint penalty counts are reproduced; finite exhaustion is sufficient because the theorem is only about this 27-vertex graph. Standalone code and orbit table provide exact reproductions; no infinite claim is inferred.

value.rationale: H(3,3) is the smallest nonbinary 3-factor Hamming graph and a canonical fixed finite monitoring network, rather than an arbitrary induced subgraph. Exact optimum-triple signatures and their reconfiguration metrics address a natural sensor relocation question not answered by power-domination-number results. The sharp three-move locality penalty, exact 41148 attaining pairs, different 3/6 radii and uniquely paired jump-distance-four configurations distinguish unconstrained and physically local monitoring changes. These are complete nontrivial invariants for a motivated symmetric test case, with clear interpretation and reproducibility; no unwarranted infinite generalization is asserted.
